summary: This note describes the 2010 FIFA World Cup, the 19th men's national football world championship, held in South Africa from 11 June to 11 July 2010. FIFA chose South Africa over Egypt and Morocco in 2004, making it the first African host of the finals. Spain beat the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time in the final, with Andrés Iniesta scoring in the 116th minute, and the note also covers the first-round exits of the hosts, Italy, France and New Zealand.
one_line: Account of the 2010 FIFA World Cup in South Africa, won by Spain with a 1-0 extra-time final victory over the Netherlands.
key_facts: The 2010 FIFA World Cup was the 19th FIFA World Cup, the world championship for men's national association football teams.
The 2010 FIFA World Cup took place in South Africa from 11 June to 11 July 2010.
The bidding process for hosting the tournament finals was open only to African nations.
In 2004, FIFA selected South Africa over Egypt and Morocco to become the first African nation to host the finals.
Spain defeated the Netherlands 1-0 after extra time in the final.
Andrés Iniesta's goal in the 116th minute gave Spain their first world title.
Spain became the eighth nation to win the tournament and the first European nation to win a World Cup hosted outside its home continent.
All World Cups held outside Europe before 2010 had been won by South American nations.
Spain is the only national team since 1978 to win a World Cup after losing a game in the group stage.
As a result of winning, Spain represented the World in the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup.
Host nation South Africa, 2006 champions Italy and 2006 runners-up France were all eliminated in the first round.
It was the first time that the hosts had been eliminated in the first round of a World Cup.
New Zealand, with their three draws, were the only undefeated team in the tournament, but they were also eliminated in the first round.
Cameroon, Denmark, Nigeria, Slovenia, South Africa and Uruguay returned after missing the 2006 tournament.
